subject: Files
notes: SHARING WITH ALL OTHER, and the two closing paragraphs the standard attaches to this item. 'allows concurrent access to a physical file through other file connectors specifying input, I-O, or extend mode, subject to any further restrictions that apply' -- the AllOther rows/columns of Table 19 (OpenTable19.cs#Cell), and FileShare.ReadWrite as the 9.1.15 file lock (FileLockPosture.OfSharingMode). 'Record locks are in effect' -- FileRegistry.LocksEffective. The paragraph 'Multiple paths of access may exist in the same runtime element, contained elements, separate runtime elements within the same run unit, or runtime elements in different run units' is the reason the file lock and the Table-19 arbitration are TWO mechanisms and not one: a host share mode names no requester, so it cannot admit this run unit's second connector while refusing a foreign process. kb/Work PB740 measured what one boolean cost: two clause-less connectors that Table 19 PERMITS to share one physical file (OPEN INPUT F-A then OPEN EXTEND F-B) were refused by the host handle and the second OPEN answered '30' -- a status no Table 19 row and no 9.1.13.9 item produces -- and the appended record was never written. FileLockPosture derives each connector's posture from its arbitrated sharing mode and widens it to admit every connector Table 19 has admitted, and FileRegistry.SyncHostPostures re-derives the whole set whenever it changes. The widening is BOUNDED, which is what keeps this rule from spending rules 1) and 2): the host checks a new handle against every outstanding one, so the run unit's lock against the outside is the INTERSECTION of its connectors' postures (unit:FileLockPostureDriftTests.WideningForASiblingDoesNotAdmitAnOutsider_AndIsGivenBackAtTheClose measures that an outside writer is still refused while the widened pair is open, and that the posture narrows back at the CLOSE -- 9.1.15, 'The file lock is removed by an explicit or implicit CLOSE statement executed for that file connector'). Goldens: pb740_clauseless_share leg L1 (both opens '00', the WRITE '00', and the INPUT connector's own file position indicator surviving the sibling's arrival) and leg L3 (two appenders, neither record lost -- 14.9.51.4 GR19 leaves only their ORDER undefined, which is why the leg counts and searches). COBOL-85 has no SHARING clause. ⛔ THE KEYED HALF IS NOW CLOSED (kb/Work PB771), so the scope note this row carried is replaced rather than kept. §9.1.15 3) names no organization and §9.1.6 says there are three, so all three owe the file lock; RELATIVE and INDEXED held no long-lived host handle at all between OPEN and CLOSE and therefore established none. MEASURED before the fix, on this tree: with a SHARING WITH NO OTHER connector holding an INDEXED (and again a RELATIVE) file open I-O, another run unit's 4-byte append SUCCEEDED, and the CLOSE then rewrote the file from the OPEN's snapshot (46->50->46 bytes indexed, 28->32->28 relative) with '00' reported on both sides. KeyedConnector.TakeFileLock now takes the connector's own HostFile.OpenConnectorStream handle on every OpenCore arm that has a physical file, carrying the posture FileLockPosture derived; RecordFraming.ReadStore/WriteStore take that STREAM rather than a path, so the store's load and persist travel through the lock instead of around it (a second handle would ask for access the connector's own FileShare.None forbids -- kb/Work PB713); ReleaseFileLock gives it back at the CLOSE and at an unsuccessful OPEN (FileConnector.AbandonOpen), and KeyedConnector.Reposture rebuilds it when the admitted set changes. unit:FileLockPostureDriftTests.EveryOrganizationHoldsALiveFileLockWhileOpen measures the lock from a handle OUTSIDE the connector for every (organization x open mode) and measures the give-back at the CLOSE; the same class's TheFileLockIsTheSharingMode_MeasuredFromOutsideTheConnector and TheHostHandleNeverVetoesWhatTable19Permits now carry the organization axis too (4 of 9 arms, and 24 cells of the matrix, were RED on the pre-fix tree). conformance:cases/9.1.15-Sharing-mode/pb771_keyed_file_lock_2023 and its 2002 twin certify the half a COBOL program can observe: the gate INSIDE the run unit is still the file connectors and Table 19, for both keyed organizations, which a new handle could silently have broken. || UPDATED (kb/Work PB322, w1013m): the widening this row's earlier notes describe (FileLockPosture.For, FileRegistry.SyncHostPostures / PostureOf and the handle rebuild) existed only for the undetermined implementor default and is DELETED. Every connector now holds one of the three modes, every pair Table 19 admits has mutually admissible base postures (EveryNormalOpenCellHasMutuallyAdmissiblePostures), and SharedOpenAttempt hands each connector the posture of its own mode before its handle exists.
